subsystems.name: Inner code block
subsystems.role: The lowest-level quantum error-correcting code, protecting one logical qubit against physical errors.

subsystems.name: Outer concatenation layer
subsystems.role: Treats each qubit of an inner block as a logical qubit and encodes it again in another code block, repeating to form a hierarchy.

subsystems.name: Syndrome extraction and decoding hierarchy
subsystems.role: Measures error syndromes at each level and passes corrected results upward so outer decoders see cleaner data.

subsystems.name: Fault-tolerant logical operations
subsystems.role: Performs gates on encoded qubits without letting a single fault spread into multiple errors within a code block.

subsystems.name: Physical qubit and control infrastructure
subsystems.role: Provides the raw qubits, gates and measurements whose error rates must stay below the code's threshold.

buildSteps.title: Choose the inner code
buildSteps.detail: Select a small stabilizer code, such as a 5-qubit or 7-qubit code, based on which physical errors dominate on the target hardware.

buildSteps.title: Set the concatenation depth
buildSteps.detail: Decide how many levels to stack and which outer code wraps the inner one, trading physical-qubit count for a lower logical error rate.

buildSteps.title: Synthesize fault-tolerant circuits
buildSteps.detail: Compile encoding, syndrome extraction and correction circuits so that one physical fault cannot create two errors in the same code block.

buildSteps.title: Build and calibrate the qubit array
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate the physical qubits, tune gates and measurements, and verify that error rates sit below the code's threshold.

buildSteps.title: Implement the inner decoder
buildSteps.detail: Run a fast decoder that keeps pace with repeated syndrome extraction at the innermost level.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate level-1 break-even
buildSteps.detail: Show that one encoded logical qubit lives longer than the best physical qubit on the same device.

buildSteps.title: Add a second level
buildSteps.detail: Concatenate again and measure whether the logical error rate falls by orders of magnitude as more levels are added.

buildSteps.title: Add non-Clifford operations
buildSteps.detail: Use magic-state distillation or code switching so the encoded qubits can run universal quantum algorithms, not just Clifford gates.

buildSteps.title: Scale to many logical qubits
buildSteps.detail: Replicate the hierarchical blocks, connect them with fault-tolerant gates, and operate a logical processor under real-time decoding.

prerequisites.tech: Physical error rates below the concatenation threshold
prerequisites.why: Concatenated codes typically need physical error rates around 10^-4 to 10^-3 depending on the code and decoder; current two-qubit gate errors are near that range but not uniformly below it.
Repeated syndrome extraction requires measurement and reset errors well below the gate error rate, which is still a challenge on many platforms.
The innermost decoder must run in real time, and outer decoders must handle many blocks without becoming a bottleneck.
Magic-state distillation has been demonstrated at small scale, but its overhead is large and it is not yet integrated into a full logical processor.
Concatenation needs many physical qubits per logical qubit, so crosstalk, wiring density and connectivity become limiting engineering problems.

pathway.milestone: Repeated syndrome extraction and break-even demonstrations on small qubit arrays
pathway.unlocks: Confidence that basic quantum error correction can preserve information longer than a physical qubit.

pathway.milestone: A level-1 concatenated logical qubit with lower error than the best physical qubit on the same device
pathway.unlocks: A working building block that can be stacked into deeper concatenation.

pathway.milestone: Two-level concatenation showing logical error rate falling by orders of magnitude
pathway.unlocks: Experimental proof of exponential error suppression in a real hierarchical code.

pathway.milestone: Fault-tolerant logical processors with enough logical qubits and non-Clifford gates for practical algorithms
pathway.unlocks: Reliable quantum simulation of chemistry and materials, where concatenation or its descendants protect the computation.
